questions.question: Which red-eye presentation needs urgent ophthalmic or emergency evaluation?
choices: Mild bilateral itching during pollen season with normal vision
Contact-lens-associated painful red eye with photophobia and reduced vision
A stable dry-eye sensation improved by lubricants
A resolved episode of morning crusting
questions.explanation: Pain, photophobia, reduced visual acuity, and contact-lens use can signal keratitis or another vision-threatening process and require urgent assessment.

questions.question: Why should topical ocular anesthetics not be prescribed for routine home pain control?
choices: They are useful only for eye-color testing
They can mask worsening injury and impair corneal healing
They always cure corneal infection
They have no effect on pain
questions.explanation: Topical anesthetics are useful for clinical examination but are not routine outpatient analgesics because they can mask deterioration and harm the cornea.

questions.question: What is a key FNP action for a patient using chronic glaucoma drops?
choices: Assume a refill proves correct use
Assess adherence, administration technique, access barriers, and systemic adverse effects
Stop drops whenever the eye is comfortable
Use multiple drops at the same time without spacing
questions.explanation: Glaucoma is often asymptomatic, and technique, access, and adverse effects strongly affect adherence and vision protection.

questions.question: Which symptom cluster suggests acute angle-closure glaucoma?
choices: Sudden blurred vision, severe eye pain/headache, nausea or vomiting, and red eye
Chronic painless stable refractive error
Mild seasonal sneezing
A painless freckle on the eyelid
questions.explanation: Acute angle closure is a time-sensitive vision emergency that may present with severe pain/headache, nausea, red eye, and visual change.

questions.question: What is a core safety consideration before recommending an oral decongestant?
choices: Only whether the patient prefers capsules
Blood pressure, arrhythmia/cardiovascular risk, insomnia, urinary symptoms, glaucoma context, and interacting medications
Whether the patient has a seasonal allergy diagnosis
Whether saline spray was tried once
questions.explanation: Systemic decongestants can affect cardiovascular, sleep, urinary, and other systems. OTC availability does not make them universally safe.

questions.question: Which acute rhinosinusitis pattern best supports possible bacterial disease rather than an uncomplicated viral URI?
choices: Symptoms improving after five days
Persistent symptoms without improvement for more than 10 days, severe presentation, or worsening after initial improvement
A single day of clear rhinorrhea
Itching after pet exposure
questions.explanation: Severe, persistent, or double-worsening patterns are clinical criteria that can support bacterial rhinosinusitis assessment; most acute cases are viral.

questions.question: Why should antibiotics not be prescribed automatically for colored nasal discharge early in a URI?
choices: Color alone proves fungal disease
Most acute rhinosinusitis is viral, and antibiotic decisions require clinical bacterial criteria
Antibiotics treat allergic rhinitis best
All upper-airway symptoms require imaging first
questions.explanation: Colored mucus alone does not establish bacterial infection. Antibiotic stewardship requires a diagnostic pattern and patient-specific assessment.

questions.question: What should be assessed before choosing otic medication?
choices: Canal and tympanic-membrane findings, diagnosis, severity, and high-risk host factors
Only the patient’s preferred ear
Whether the patient owns headphones
Whether the patient requests an antibiotic
questions.explanation: Otic therapy depends on the cause of ear symptoms and tympanic-membrane status; high-risk infection can require urgent escalation.

questions.question: Which otitis externa presentation is especially concerning?
choices: Mild itch after swimming without pain
Severe ear pain with diabetes, granulation tissue, or cranial-nerve findings
A normal canal examination
Brief pressure change during air travel
questions.explanation: Severe pain and high-risk features in a patient with diabetes or immune compromise can signal invasive disease and need urgent evaluation.

questions.question: What is an appropriate counseling point when multiple chronic eye drops are prescribed at the same time?
choices: Instill them simultaneously to save time
Separate drops so one does not wash out the other and review technique
Use an extra drop whenever any is missed
Stop all drops when vision seems stable
questions.explanation: Spacing different eye drops and confirming proper technique supports medication delivery and adherence.
